title: Northwatch claims routing - field notes
content:
Call date: 2025-11-03
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood), Marco (Redwood SE), Samantha (Northwatch - Head of Claims Ops), Owen (Northwatch - Infra), Priya (Vendor integrator)

Purpose: quick-sync after POC run; capture production constraints + immediate next steps. Mostly a scratchpad — messy, prioritized capture.

HIGHLIGHTS / TL;DR
- Northwatch wants a lightweight LLM-based triage layer to route incoming claim intake to correct internal queues + assign urgency score.
- Hard constraints: sub-250ms median inference for short text (<=120 tokens), HIPAA-adjacent PII controls (they treat claims like PHI), and fully auditable input handling (KMS + audit log).
- Strong preference for private deployment inside their VPC, but open to Hybrid (hosted control plane + private inference) if it speeds time-to-value.

RAW NOTES (transcribed)
- Samantha: "We need near real-time. If it slows agents down they'll turn it off."
- Owen: "Network egress is a showstopper; we can't send raw claim text outside our VPC. Tokenization or redaction in-flight isn't allowed by compliance."
- Priya: "We can do a preprocessor to strip PHI but it must be reversible for audit — or better, send a mapping token."

Functional requirements (as captured)
- Input: unstructured claim text + optional attachments metadata (MIME types).
- Outputs: classification label (auto: 'auto-approve' | 'review' | 'escalate'), queue destination tag, urgency score 0-100, structured breakdown of entities (policy id, provider name, date) for downstream routing.
- Confidence + tokenized excerpt that triggered decision for audit.

Non-functional / SLA
- Latency: p50 <= 250ms; p95 <= 800ms for typical 60–120 token requests.
- Throughput: baseline 60 req/s with spikes to 300 req/s for incident windows; burst handling without dropping SLA.
- Availability: 99.9% for triage endpoint.
- Data residency: inference must occur in their us-east-1 VPC. No replica outside.

Security & Compliance notes
- Must integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS) for any key material.
- Audit trail required per request: input hash, model version, route decision, RO metadata (who/when).
- No model updates without explicit versioned rollout + canary; they require 'frozen' model for 30 days after a rollout in prod.

Architecture sketch (rough)
- Option A (preferred by Northwatch): Redwood Private, control plane in Redwood, inference nodes in customer VPC (private RBAC) + egress firewall rules.
- Option B (quicker MVP): Hosted Redwood API + preprocessor inside VPC sends de-identified payloads. Must validate de-id mapping and audit chain.

Kernel / performance considerations (internal notes)
- Suggest model: redwood-13B-quant (or smaller distilled variant) to hit latency targets — need perf bench on their typical token distributions.
- KV cache savings: their inbound claims often re-use templates; suggest enabling prefix caching for known boilerplate to reduce cost.
- Batching: keep disabled for p50-sensitive path; consider micro-batching (10ms window) only for non-blocking background scoring.

Gotchas observed / flagged by Northwatch
- Attachments: optical text extraction (OCR) adds variability; OCR runs upstream but sometimes misses linebreaks -> impacts token counts.
- PII redaction: they expect reversible mapping for audit which is awkward for hosted de-identification.
- Model hallucination risk on entities (provider names) — they require conservative extract + fall back to manual triage if entity confidence < 0.7.

Quick wins we proposed in call
- Ship a canary with Hosted API + preprocessor (Option B) for 2-week live shadowing to measure latency & entity-extract F1. Non-blocking: don't return decisions to agents until validated.
- Add a tiny regression test harness: 200 golden prompts from their historical claims to measure routing accuracy, token counts, and perf.

Concrete next steps (owner, due)
- Aisha: produce perf benchmark plan + request sample payload set (anon) from Northwatch — due 2025-11-10.
- Marco: sketch Private deployment diagram + KMS integration checklist — due 2025-11-07.
- Samantha/Owen: confirm acceptable de-id mapping approach and legal on reversible mappings — due 2025-11-14.
- Priya: share OCR preprocess notes + sample attachments (redacted) — due 2025-11-08.

Short-term questions to resolve
- Can Northwatch accept a hosted control plane with inference-only nodes in VPC? (SLA/contract implications)
- What is acceptable retention window for raw inputs inside Redwood logs (if any) for auditing?
- Are there rate-limit burst allowances tied to their incident windows? (we need allowances in Dedicated capacity config)

Notes to self (Aisha)
- Prep a lightweight eval: precision/recall + iso-latency buckets (0-200ms, 200-500ms, 500-1s).
- Check whether redwood-13B-quant supports HSM-backed key access for KV encryption at-rest in Private. If not, call SRE infra.
- Draft compliance FAQ for reversible de-id pattern (legal approved language).

Loose brainstorm (non-polished)
- Could return a short deterministic token that maps to stored full PHI in their VPC (token references only used inside VPC) — keeps decisioning model blind to raw PHI. Need mapping store + strong auth.
- Fallback policy idea: if entity confidence < 0.7 OR latency > 800ms -> route to 'manual triage' queue + create audit ticket automatically.

Misc references / links mentioned on call
- NW historical sample set location (internal): s3://northwatch-prod/claims/samples/pooled-2024-2025 (asked them to give read-only access to aishap@redwood)
- Jira: NW-2345 for integration workstream
- Slack channel: #northwatch-pilot (watch for Priya notes)

Status: actionable draft. This should be converted into a one-pager for legal + a separate perf plan doc.

TODO (short)
- [ ] Get anonymized sample JSON (50–200 records) from Northwatch (Aisha).
- [ ] Internal perf bench with redwood-13B-quant on 1xA100 to estimate p95 for median 90-token workloads (Marco).
- [ ] Draft Private deployment checklist (KMS, VPC peering, subnets, IAM) and share with Owen.

End of scratch capture — will tidy into a customer-facing pilot brief once answers come back.
